title: Cohomological dimension of a smooth affine curve
statement:
For a smooth affine connected curve $C$
over an algebraically closed field and any torsion
etale sheaf $F$,
one has $H^q(C,F)=0$ for $q>1$, with cohomology as in
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: For $q\geq3$, the vanishing follows from [lem-sc-cohomological-dimension], since the hypotheses on $C$ imply that it is a smooth separated connected curve. For $q=2$: $C$ is of finite type over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; every local ring $\mathcal O_{C,P}$ is regular by [lem-sc-smooth-regular], so $C$ is a regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme]; being nonempty and connected, $C$ is integral by [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral]. Let $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}k(C)\to C$ be its generic point and set $M=\eta^*F$. $M$ is torsion by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-torsion], so [lem-sc-generic-cohomology-comparison] (for the smooth integral separated curve $C$) identifies $H^2(C,F)$ with $H^2(C,\eta_*M)$. The latter group vanishes by [lem-sc-affine-generic-second], applied to the smooth integral affine connected curve $C$ and to $M$.
